attribution: The correction growth is attributable to posture drift away from the frozen step-0 reference, not to hazard proximity. The Safety-CVAE was trained on raw absolute skin depths, so its output is a strong function of how much static structure is in view; the number of active sensors more than doubles as the arm enters the fumehood cavity. Subtracting a reference captured at the step-0 posture therefore leaves a large residual that reflects the posture change. This is a direct consequence of using mode B (first_live_skin) rather than the documented mode D (per-frame frame-aligned parked-obstacle counterfactual), which by construction cancels the static contribution at the CURRENT posture.

actual_hazard_proximity.evidence: zero hazard-bar (body protr_*) contact frames in the entire episode; the bar was never touched

changing_self_returns.evidence: the two known self-return sensors link5_front_sensor_1 and link5_front_sensor_2 were active in 0 of 200 frames

changing_static_fumehood_returns.evidence: active sensors grow 10 -> 22 as the arm enters the cavity (by step: [10, 9, 15, 17, 20, 17, 20, 21, 21, 22]); 12 sensors newly activate across links 2,3,4,5_back,5_front,6 by step 100

posture_drift_from_the_frozen_reference.evidence: the reference is head(skin at step-0 posture) and never updates, while the arm traverses into the cavity. raw |head| swings 0.112 .. 2.134 with posture alone, so the difference raw-minus-frozen-reference measures how far the posture has moved from step 0, not how close the hazard is.

target_grasp_contact.evidence: grasp-target contacts appear only intermittently and do not coincide with the correction's rise; the rise begins by step 20, well before any contact

caveat: ONE episode. This attributes a mechanism; it does not measure an effect size and supports no claim about the controller's merit.
